newsitem.title: UK: UK's Rifkind calls for end to Jew row with Germany. [CORRECTED 13:10 GMT 23/2]
newsitem.headline: UK's Rifkind calls for end to Jew row with Germany. [CORRECTED 13:10 GMT 23/2]

text.p: British Foreign Secretary Malcolm Rifkind called on Sunday for a row to be dropped over Jewish remarks about him in a German newspaper.
He issued his plea after outrage in Britain over a report in Thursday's Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung (corrects day)
Germany's embassy in London was reported to have been flooded with protest calls and several British politicians said they were appalled at what one called "the language of Hitler".
But Rifkind made clear he regarded the matter as closed.
"I have no intention of pressing the matter, nor would I want anyone else to do so," he told the Sunday Telegraph newspaper.
"It was a rather silly remark by a young journalist who herself has said she is mortified by the interpretation that has been put on it," he added.
German journalist Michaela Wiegel, writing about a speech made by Rifkind in Bonn last week, had concluded in the newspaper:

"As if he was not completely convinced by his own words, the Jew Rifkind concluded -- ironically, apologetically -- with a quote from Luther, delivered in German, Here I stand. I cannot do otherwise.'"
Both Wiegel and the newspaper have declined to apologise saying no offence was intended.
But the remark dominated news bulletins on Saturday and did nothing to heal latent distrust of Germany in Britain that dates back to World War Two.
Former Conservative cabinet minister David Hunt said he had written to the president of the German parliament.

"This is back to the language of Hitler. We must not allow anyone to lapse back into that disgraceful terminology," said Hunt, who is also chairman of the British branch of the inter-parliamentary Council Against Anti-Semitism.
Rifkind's family moved to Scotland from Lithuania in the 19th century. He is one of two Jewish cabinet ministers, along with Michael Howard, the Home Secretary.
Former Labour minister Gerald Kaufman was horrified.
"I was absolutely appalled when I saw it. I had thought this kind of thing was all over in Germany these days. Words fail me. I cannot express my revulsion strongly enough," he said.
And Sir Ivan Lawrence, a member of the Board of Deputies of British Jews, said: "This is not only offensive to the foreign secretary, it is offensive to the United Kingdom."
